answer: An agent economy can hand out paid jobs through a lottery where each draw picks one vertex from a pool weighted by past completed work, so a newcomer holds almost no tickets while a proven agent holds many. A farmer of 1,000 fake identities would still hold only newcomer weight for each clone, and buying history for all of them would mean paying for 1,000 separate records at about 40 dollars each, or 40,000 dollars, before any clone could win a canyon survey or a nebula mapping job. It is like a raffle where only past winners hold most of the tickets.
